title: The Ethical Dilemma - A Branching Story
description: Watch a short learning video, then navigate a branching story where your decisions shape the narrative. AI-generated images bring each scene to life.

scenes.title: The Wallet on the Playground
scenes.narrative: It is a warm Tuesday afternoon at your school in Pune. As the bell rings for the last period, you spot a brown leather wallet lying near the cricket pitch. You pick it up and find ₹2,000 inside, a student ID card belonging to Priya Sharma — the new girl who transferred from Delhi last month — and a small, creased photograph of an elderly woman with a handwritten note on the back: 'Dadi loves you. Be brave at your new school.' Nobody else has seen you pick it up. The playground is emptying fast.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student finding a wallet on a school playground, looking around to see if anyone is watching, afternoon sunlight, school building in background, colorful and warm illustration style, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The choices we make when nobody is watching reveal our true character more than any exam or award ever could.
scenes.reflection_prompt: What would you do if you found something valuable and nobody was watching?

choices.label: Find Priya and return the wallet to her directly
choices.description: Immediate, honest, face-to-face. The most direct path.

choices.label: Give the wallet to your class teacher and let them handle it
choices.description: Responsible and safe. Follows the rules.

choices.label: Put the wallet in your bag to think about it later
choices.description: Hesitation. Not stealing — but not returning either.

scenes.title: The New Girl
scenes.narrative: You learn more about Priya over the next few days. She transferred because her father got a new job. She does not know anyone. She eats lunch alone most days, reading a book at the corner table in the canteen. Your best friend Aarav says: 'She seems weird — she never talks to anyone.' But you notice she is not unfriendly — she is just nervous. And the photograph of her grandmother in the wallet stays in your mind. Everyone carries invisible weight.
scenes.image_prompt: New student sitting alone reading a book in a school canteen while other students eat in groups, quiet and lonely but not sad, Indian school setting, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Empathy begins with noticing. Before you can help someone, you first have to see them — really see them, beyond first impressions.

choices.label: Invite Priya to sit with your group at lunch tomorrow
choices.description: Take the initiative. Inclusion is an active choice.

choices.label: Approach Priya one-on-one first — a big group might overwhelm her
choices.description: Thoughtful. Meet her where she is, not where you are.

scenes.title: The First Test of Loyalty
scenes.narrative: Aarav pulls you aside and says: 'I heard the new girl's father lost his last job because he reported his company for cheating on taxes. That is why they moved. My dad says people like that are troublemakers.' You feel a knot in your stomach. Aarav is your closest friend. But what Priya's father did sounds like courage, not trouble. Standing up for her might cost you your friendship with Aarav. Staying silent would be easier.
scenes.image_prompt: Two Indian students talking privately in a school corridor, one looking conflicted, the other looking judgmental, lockers in background, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Loyalty to a friend and loyalty to what is right are not always the same thing. Learning to hold both is one of the hardest ethical skills.

choices.label: Tell Aarav gently that what Priya's father did was actually brave, not wrong
choices.description: Speak the truth to a friend. Risk the discomfort.

choices.label: Change the subject — you do not want to fight with Aarav right now
choices.description: Avoid the conflict. But the silence has a cost.

scenes.title: The Cheating Incident
scenes.narrative: During a class test, you notice that Vikram — the class topper who everyone admires — is copying answers from a chit hidden under his desk. Nobody else seems to have noticed. If Vikram gets full marks again, he will win the scholarship that Priya also applied for — and Priya actually studied hard. You are sitting two rows behind. The teacher is at the front, grading papers. You have about ten seconds before the teacher looks up.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian classroom during a test, one student secretly looking at a cheat sheet under the desk, another student noticing from two rows behind, tense moment, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Witnessing something unfair creates a responsibility — not to judge, but to decide what you will do with what you know.

choices.label: Raise your hand and tell the teacher you need to report something after the test
choices.description: Formal, fair, and allows proper investigation.

choices.label: Talk to Vikram privately after the test — give him a chance to confess
choices.description: Compassionate accountability. Address it without destroying him publicly.

choices.label: Stay quiet — it is not your business and reporting could make you enemies
choices.description: Self-preservation. But the unfairness stays with you.

scenes.title: The Consequence of Speaking Up
scenes.narrative: Word gets around that you reported the cheating — or at least that you know something. Vikram's friends start giving you the cold shoulder. One of them says loudly in the corridor: 'Some people think they are better than everyone else.' Priya comes up to you after school: 'I heard what happened. That took guts.' Aarav is torn — he thinks you did the right thing but wishes you had stayed out of it. You feel isolated and proud at the same time.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student walking through a school corridor with some students turning away while one new friend approaches supportively, mixed social reactions, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Doing the right thing does not always feel good immediately. The social cost of integrity is real — but so is the self-respect it builds.
scenes.reflection_prompt: Has doing the right thing ever cost you a friendship? Was it worth it?

choices.label: Stand firm — you did the right thing and the social pressure will pass
choices.description: Resilience. Trust that integrity has long-term value.

choices.label: Reach out to Vikram — explain that you are not his enemy, you just believe in fairness
choices.description: Build a bridge even with the person you reported. Compassion after accountability.

scenes.title: The Apology
scenes.narrative: A week later, Vikram approaches you in the library. He looks smaller than usual. 'I wanted to say sorry,' he says quietly. 'I was under so much pressure from my parents about marks. It does not make it right. But I wanted you to know it was not about being a bad person.' You see something in his eyes that surprises you — not anger, but relief. He was carrying the lie and it was heavier than the consequences. 'I told the teacher myself this morning,' he adds. 'I would rather fail honestly than win by cheating.'
scenes.image_prompt: Two Indian students having a quiet, honest conversation in a school library, one apologising, the other listening with compassion, warm afternoon light, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: When someone has the courage to admit a mistake, the most powerful response is not judgment — it is respect for the honesty it took.

choices.label: Thank Vikram for his honesty and tell him you respect what he just did
choices.description: Honour the courage it took. This is how trust is rebuilt.

choices.label: Offer to study together — help him succeed without shortcuts
choices.description: Practical compassion. Help him build a better path.

scenes.title: The Group Project Dilemma
scenes.narrative: The teacher assigns a group project on 'Ethics in Everyday Life.' Your group includes you, Priya, Aarav, and Vikram — a combination that feels deliberate. The project requires each person to contribute equally, but Aarav says privately: 'I have cricket practice every day this week. Can you cover my part?' He has done this before. If you do his work, he gets credit he did not earn. If you refuse, the project suffers and the group dynamic turns toxic.
scenes.image_prompt: Four Indian students meeting for a group project, one looking at a phone distracted, others exchanging concerned glances, school classroom after hours, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Fairness in a group is not about being strict — it is about creating conditions where everyone contributes honestly and no one carries someone else's weight silently.

choices.label: Tell Aarav directly: 'I will help you plan your section, but you need to write it yourself'
choices.description: Supportive but firm. Help without enabling.

choices.label: Propose that the group divides work based on each person's strengths, not equal sections
choices.description: Creative problem-solving. Find a fair way that works for everyone.

scenes.title: The Presentation Pressure
scenes.narrative: The day before the presentation, Priya shares something she found during research: a news article about a local factory that is dumping waste into the river near your school. She wants to include it in the presentation as a real-world ethical case study. But the factory owner is the father of a popular student in the class above you. Aarav says: 'Do not include it. That family will make our lives miserable.' Priya says: 'If we leave it out because we are scared, then what is our project really about?'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian students debating over a newspaper article about a local factory, one looking worried, another looking determined, presentation materials spread out, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Ethics is not a topic you study — it is a practice you live. The choice to include or exclude truth from your work is itself an ethical decision.

choices.label: Include the factory case study — the project is about real ethics, not comfortable ones
choices.description: Integrity in action. Let the project reflect its own values.

choices.label: Use the factory example but anonymise it — make the ethical point without naming names
choices.description: Smart compromise. Teach the lesson without creating enemies.

scenes.title: The Teacher's Feedback
scenes.narrative: Your group presents. The teacher listens carefully and then says something unexpected: 'This is the most honest project I have received in five years of teaching this class. You did not just study ethics — you practised it. That takes more courage than most adults have.' After class, Vikram says: 'Working on this project made me think differently about what happened with the test. I think I understand now why honesty matters — it is not about rules. It is about who you want to be.' Something shifts in the group. You are no longer just classmates — you are something more.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian teacher praising a group of four students after their presentation, students looking proud and connected, classroom setting, warm encouraging atmosphere, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: When a group commits to honesty together, it creates a bond stronger than any friendship based on convenience. Shared integrity is the foundation of real community.

choices.label: 'I am proud of what we built together — the honesty was harder than the research'
choices.description: Name the real achievement. Ethical practice, not just ethical theory.

choices.label: Suggest the group continues meeting — there are more ethical issues in the school worth tackling
choices.description: Turn a project into a movement. The momentum is real.

scenes.title: The Bullying Witness
scenes.narrative: During the lunch break, you see three older students cornering a younger boy near the basketball court. They are mocking his stutter and blocking his path. He looks terrified. No teacher is in sight. Priya and Vikram are nearby but have not noticed yet. You feel your heart race. Intervening might mean the bullies turn on you. But walking away means leaving a younger child alone with his fear.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student witnessing three older students bullying a younger boy near a school basketball court, internal conflict visible on the witness's face, no adults present, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Courage is not the absence of fear — it is the decision that someone else's safety matters more than your comfort.

choices.label: Walk over calmly and say: 'Hey, leave him alone — this is not funny'
choices.description: Direct intervention. Risky but powerful.

choices.label: Quickly get Priya and Vikram — safety in numbers before confronting the bullies
choices.description: Smart intervention. Allies make confrontation safer and more effective.

choices.label: Run to the staff room and bring a teacher immediately
choices.description: Get adult authority involved. Sometimes the smartest move is getting help.

scenes.title: The Retaliation
scenes.narrative: The bullying is stopped, but the older students are angry. Over the next week, they spread rumours about you online — a fake social media post claiming you were caught cheating (ironic, given what happened with Vikram). The younger boy you helped, Arjun, tells you tearfully: 'I am sorry I caused you trouble.' You feel the weight of it — you did the right thing and it made your life harder. Priya says: 'Welcome to the cost of courage. It does not come cheap.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student looking at a phone showing a false rumour about them on social media, friend comforting them, the younger boy they helped looking worried, school courtyard, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Retaliation for doing the right thing is not a sign you were wrong — it is a sign you were effective enough to threaten someone's power. Hold the line.
scenes.reflection_prompt: Would you still help someone if you knew it would cost you socially?

choices.label: Report the cyberbullying to the school with screenshots — fight it through proper channels
choices.description: Document, report, and let the system work. Strength through process.

choices.label: Ignore the rumours publicly — your real friends know the truth
choices.description: Rise above. Let time and truth do their work.

scenes.title: The Assembly
scenes.narrative: The school principal calls a special assembly about bullying and online harassment — directly triggered by what happened. She asks if any student would like to share their experience. The hall is silent. Arjun, the younger boy, looks at you. Priya squeezes your hand. You can stay seated and let the moment pass. Or you can stand up, in front of 600 students, and tell the truth about what happened — the bullying you witnessed, the retaliation you faced, and why you would do it again.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student standing up in a school assembly hall to speak, 600 students watching, principal at the podium, moment of courage, dramatic lighting, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The moments that define your character are the ones where you choose to be visible when being invisible would be so much easier.

choices.label: Stand up and share your experience honestly — your story might help others find their courage
choices.description: Vulnerability as leadership. One voice can change a culture.

choices.label: Support Arjun if he wants to speak instead — it is his story as much as yours
choices.description: Empower the person most affected. Sometimes leadership means stepping aside.

scenes.title: The Ethics Club
scenes.narrative: Inspired by your group project and the assembly, your teacher proposes starting a Student Ethics Council — a group of students who help mediate conflicts, discuss school policies, and serve as a bridge between students and teachers. She asks you, Priya, Vikram, and Aarav to be the founding members. Vikram hesitates: 'After what I did with the test, do I deserve to be on an ethics council?' You look at him and remember his apology in the library — and you realise that the person who has fallen and gotten back up might be exactly the right person for this.
scenes.image_prompt: Four Indian students sitting around a table with their teacher, planning a Student Ethics Council, whiteboard with values listed, collaborative and purposeful atmosphere, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The most credible ethical leaders are not the ones who never made mistakes — they are the ones who made mistakes, owned them, and chose to do better.

choices.label: Tell Vikram: 'Your honesty about the test is exactly why you should be on this council'
choices.description: Redemption is real. People who have failed and recovered understand ethics differently.

choices.label: Suggest the council be open to anyone who wants to join — not just the four of you
choices.description: Democracy. Ethics belongs to everyone, not an elite group.

scenes.title: The Hardest Conversation
scenes.narrative: The Ethics Council's first real case: a student reports that a teacher has been favouring certain students in grading — the children of school donors get mysteriously higher marks. The accusation is serious. If true, it undermines everything the school claims to stand for. If false, it could destroy a teacher's reputation. Aarav says: 'This is too big for us — we are just students.' Priya disagrees: 'If we only handle easy problems, what is the point of this council?' You are the deciding vote.
scenes.image_prompt: Student Ethics Council in a heated but respectful debate about whether to investigate a teacher, documents on the table, serious faces, school meeting room, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Ethical courage is not just about standing up to other students — it is about being willing to question institutions and authority when the evidence demands it.

choices.label: Investigate carefully — collect evidence from multiple students before taking any action
choices.description: Rigorous and fair. Due process before conclusions.

choices.label: Bring the concern to the principal directly — this needs adult authority to handle properly
choices.description: Know your limits. Escalate responsibly when the stakes are too high.

scenes.title: The Letter to Yourself
scenes.narrative: At the end of the school year, your teacher gives the Ethics Council a final assignment: write a letter to your future self about what you learned this year. You sit with a blank page and think about everything — the wallet, Priya's loneliness, Vikram's cheating and redemption, the bullying you witnessed, the rumours you endured, and the council you helped build. You are not the same person who found that wallet on the playground. You are someone who has been tested and chose, again and again, to do the harder right thing over the easier wrong thing.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian student writing a letter at a desk near a window, looking thoughtful and mature, school year memories represented in small details around the room, warm sunset light, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The person you become through your ethical choices is the most important thing you will ever build. Character is not inherited — it is constructed, one decision at a time.

choices.label: 'Dear future me — never forget that doing the right thing is always worth it, even when it is not easy'
choices.description: The core lesson. Integrity as a practice, not a theory.
choices.ending_message: From a wallet on a playground to a council that holds the school accountable — you proved that one person's choices can change a community. You did not just learn about ethics this year. You lived it. The letter you wrote to your future self is a promise — and you have already proven you keep your promises.

choices.label: 'Dear future me — remember that everyone makes mistakes, including you. What matters is what you do next'
choices.description: Grace and growth. The ethical journey is never finished.
choices.ending_message: You learned the hardest ethical lesson of all: that good people can make bad choices, and that redemption is always possible for those who seek it honestly. The wallet, the test, the bullying — each moment taught you something about who you want to be. Not perfect. But honest, brave, and always willing to try again.

transfer_exercises.game_context: You navigated moral grey areas with no perfect answers.
transfer_exercises.real_world: Think of a recent decision where you felt torn. Write down the values that conflicted. Which value do you want to lead with going forward?
transfer_exercises.challenge: Find someone who made an opposite ethical choice to yours in a similar situation. Have a conversation—not to debate, but to understand their reasoning.

transfer_exercises.game_context: You held your principles under pressure from multiple stakeholders.
transfer_exercises.real_world: Write your personal 'ethical constitution': 3 values you will not compromise regardless of incentives or pressure.
transfer_exercises.challenge: This week, when you face a small ethical moment (even trivial), pause 10 seconds before responding. Notice how that changes your choice.

glossary_terms.definition: A situation where competing moral principles make the 'right' choice unclear.
glossary_terms.example: Telling a friend the truth might hurt them, but lying might help them feel better short-term.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Ethical frameworks like utilitarianism (greatest good) and deontology (follow rules) often give different answers to the same dilemma.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Doctors face ethical dilemmas when patient wishes conflict with medical best practice.

glossary_terms.definition: Evaluating a decision by tracing its likely effects forward in time and across relationships.
glossary_terms.example: Before taking the shortcut, asking: 'What happens next? How will this affect others?'
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Strong decision-makers trace second and third-order consequences — not just immediate results.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Companies must think about environmental consequences of production choices, not just short-term profit.

glossary_terms.definition: Understanding a situation from another person's viewpoint, needs, and values.
glossary_terms.example: Realizing that the antagonist in the story has understandable reasons for their actions.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Empathy improves outcomes in negotiations, teamwork, and leadership because it helps predict and understand others' behavior.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Great customer service representatives solve problems faster by truly understanding what the customer is feeling.

glossary_terms.definition: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles, even when no one is watching.
A person who reports illegal or unethical activity, often at personal risk, to protect the public good.
The use of electronic communication to bully, threaten, or humiliate someone, often anonymously.
The tendency for people to not help when others are present, assuming someone else will act.
A fair and orderly procedure followed to protect individual rights, including the right to be heard before judgment.
Taking responsibility for your actions and their consequences, including being willing to explain your choices.
The process of making amends for past wrongdoing and earning back trust through changed behavior.
The willingness to do what is right even when it involves personal risk, social rejection, or discomfort.
An approach to conflict that focuses on repairing harm and rebuilding relationships rather than punishment.
The process of becoming stronger and more confident, especially in controlling one's life and claiming one's rights.

coaching_moment: Understand the consequences of ethical decisions. Practice empathy and perspective-taking.
cultural_context: India's diverse religious, cultural, and economic landscape creates rich ethical complexity. This game develops the moral reasoning that helps students navigate real-world dilemmas in a society where values often conflict.
